summary: Petition under Section 79 (1) (c) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 seeking adjudication of transmission charges by Respondent No.1, MSETCL. The present Petition is filed under Section 79 (1) (c) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 with the following prayers: - _(e) Pass such other further orders which the Hon’ble Commission may deem just in the facts and circumstances of the present case._ 3. Counsel for the Petitioner reiterated their claims as stated in the Petition. In response to the Commission's specific query on the jurisdiction of the Commission, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that the use of MSETCL's transmission lines/ system is clearly an intervening transmission system for the supply of inter-State power (330 MW) to Indian Railways. Thus, the Commission has jurisdiction in the present case under Section 79(1)(c) read with Sections 35 and 36 of the Electricity Act, 2003. 4. The Commission directed to the Petitioner to issue notice to the Respondents on the admissibility of the Petition. - (c) The Petitioner has not entered into any agreement whatsoever with the MSETCL, and hence there is no legal right to file the instant Petition against the answering Respondent. The Commission ought to dismiss the instant petition. Power is transmitted through the InSTS network of the state to various destinations of Indian Railways spread through the States of Maharashtra, Gujarat, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, Uttar Pradesh, and Karnataka. 6. Petitioner vide affidavit dated 15.03.2021 has filed a rejoinder and mainly submitted as below: _shall revise the calculation of payable transmission charges based on methodology used for calculating charges for the year 2011-12 and that shall be done as soon as possible. The Petitioner shall raise the revised bills based upon calculations done by WRPC.”_ 7. Learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) has filed Interlocutory Application No. 45 of 2021, for its impleadment in the present petition, which is opposed by the Petitioner on the grounds that MSEDCL is neither a necessary nor a proper party to the present dispute. She further submitted that the present dispute is with regard to the manner of transmission charges for the power flowing on inter-State basis using the transmission lines of MSETCL and MSETCL is charging the Petitioner as per the tariff determined by MERC in the respective years while, in the facts and circumstances of the case, MERC is not vested with the jurisdiction to determine the tariff. 13. During the hearing dated 11.08.2023, the Petitioner opposed the impleadment of MSEDCL in the case. 15. Petitioner referred to the Commission’s order dated 04.02.2021 in Petition No. 153/MP/2018 & 154/MP/2018 wherein the Commission allowed WRPC to revise the 21. Petitioner vide affidavit dated 22.09.2023 has reiterated its earlier submissions and has submitted as below: 22. The Petitioner impleaded MSEDCL and filed an amended Memo of Parties dated 28.09.2023. Further, vide Written Submissions dated 28.09.2023, have been submitted as under: 23. The Commission observed that Maharashtra State Electricity Distribution Company Limited (MSEDCL) has been impleaded by the Petitioner as Respondent No. 5 and has filed the amended ‘Memo of Parties’. Therefore, IA No. 45/IA/2021 stands disposed of. The Commission directed parties to file their Written Submission in the matter. 24. The learned counsel for MSEDCL submitted that there is no formal contract between the Petitioner and MSETCL. He further submitted that the determination of the state transmission charges is the jurisdiction of MERC. Therefore, the instant petition is not maintainable and is liable to be dismissed. The Commission directed the parties to file their written submissions in the matter by 29.4.2024, with an advance copy to each other. Subject to this the Commission reserved the Order in the matter. - (a) The Petitioner has not entered into any agreement whatsoever with the Respondent No.1 and hence has no legal right to file the instant Petition against the Respondent No.1; therefore, this Commission ought to dismiss the instant petition _in limine_ . 27. Since the order in the present Petition, which was reserved on 16.04.2024, could not be issued prior to the Members of this Commission, who formed part of the Coram, demitted office, the matter was relisted for hearing. Learned counsels for parties have submitted that the pleadings had been completed and arguments were heard, and accordingly requested the Commission to issue the Order based on the information already on record. Considering the above, the Commission reserved the matter for Order. 32. We have considered the submissions of the Petitioner and Respondents and perused all relevant documents on record. The issue that arises for our consideration is as follows: ## 34. Order dated 04.02.2021 in Petition 153/MP/2018 and 154/MP/2018 is quoted as under: _26. From a combined reading of the judgment of APTEL dated 17.12.2007 (in I.A. No. 206 and 207 in Appeal No.150 of 2007) and the Commission’s order dated 3.2.2009 (in Petition No. 64/2008 and Petition No. 67/2008), we infer that determination of tariff for use of the transmission network of a State for the purpose of wheeling of electricity to another State is within jurisdiction of the Commission in terms of Section 79(1)(c) and (d) read with Section 2(36) of the Act. That being so, the Commission also has jurisdiction to adjudicate the dispute under Section 79(1)(f) of the Act._ _27. In the instant matter, power is being transmitted to DNHED and GED from RGPPL located in the State of Maharashtra using intra-State transmission network of MSETCL and inter-State network of PGCIL and is thus, inter-State transmission of power. Therefore, adjudication of dispute in the present Petitions lies within the jurisdiction of the Commission._
title: Petition under Section 79 (1) (c) and (f) of the Electricity Act, 2003 seeking adjudication of transmission charges by Respondent No.1, MSETCL. Ratnagiri Gas and Power Private Limited
